chunks: And from him, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from 'Ali ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'We visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him); how should we establish prayer next to him?' He said, 'Stand behind him near his shoulders, then send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and send blessings upon al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer at the grave of Imam Husayn according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the specific etiquette (adab) for praying at the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), emphasizing the physical proximity to the grave by standing behind it near the shoulders. It uniquely prescribes reciting *Salat al-Nabi* followed by *Salat al-Husayn* as an integral part of the ritual prayer, reflecting the Shia tradition of honoring the Ahl al-Bayt through direct intercessory blessings. This practice underscores the theological concept of the Imams as spiritual intermediaries and the sanctity of their resting places as sites of divine connection.
